description:
Determine empirically whether Charon/Aeneas can extract a trait-generic gf2-core algorithm on the workspace MSRV, and record the outcome either way.

## Background

The current extraction covers concrete arithmetic only: the core invocation opaques `gf2_core::field`, and the prior attempt to extract generic `permanent_ryser<F>` was falsified — Charon did not monomorphise from a non-generic start root, and the direct extracted binding was descoped in favor of an abstract proof. The spike target is `batch_inverse<F: FiniteField>` (or a comparably small self-contained trait-generic gf2-core function). Vary the start roots and opaque list, including a generic start root and un-opaquing the field module for the target, and record every invocation and outcome. No proofs are authored in this issue; the proof sketch and proof implementation are planned in a follow-up round once this spike's outcome exists.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A spike record documents the exact Charon/Aeneas invocations attempted and their outcomes on the workspace MSRV toolchain.
- [hard] REQ-02: On success, the generated Lean for the generic target is preserved under the spike's extraction directory named in the record; on failure, the falsifying evidence is recorded and the required decision on the epic's extraction criterion is named for escalation.

## Notes

- Follow-on: a successful record triggers a follow-up planning round adding the approved-sketch and proof-implementation issues (sketch approved before proof code); a falsification escalates the epic's extraction criterion to the owner.
title: Spike Charon extraction of a trait-generic field algorithm
